title: LIC Q1 Results Explained: What Investors Need to Know
description: LIC reported a robust 22.8% year-on-year increase in net profit, reaching ₹13,492 crore for Q1 FY27. The Value of New Business (VNB) surged by 61.3% to ₹3,136.

faq.q: What is Value of New Business (VNB)?
faq.a: VNB represents the expected future profits from all new insurance policies sold by a company during a specific period. It's a key metric for insurance companies, indicating the profitability and quality of their new business.

faq.q: Why is VNB margin important for an insurance company?
faq.a: VNB margin shows how much value an insurer generates relative to the new business it writes. A higher VNB margin indicates that the company is selling more profitable policies, often due to a better product mix or efficient operations.

Participating (par) policies allow policyholders to share in the insurer's profits, typically through bonuses or dividends. Non-participating (non-par) policies offer guaranteed benefits without profit sharing, often with more predictable returns for the insurer.

faq.q: How does the solvency ratio impact policyholders?
faq.a: The solvency ratio indicates an insurer's financial strength and its ability to meet its obligations to policyholders. A higher solvency ratio, like LIC's 2.42, means the company has sufficient capital to pay out claims, providing greater security to policyholders.

faq.q: What does the increase in non-par products mean for LIC's future?
faq.a: LIC's increasing focus on non-par products suggests a strategic shift towards higher-margin and more predictable profit streams. This can lead to more stable earnings and improved profitability over the long term, benefiting shareholders.

First-Year Premium Income (FYPI) is the total premium collected by an insurance company from new policies sold during a financial year. It's a key indicator of an insurer's ability to attract new customers and expand its business.
